Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering and product teams reviewed Redwood's streaming demo and are interested in a formal MAP that includes concrete TTFT (time-to-first-token) and streaming latency targets at different concurrencies. High-level asks: 

- Target TTFT for 1–4 concurrent users and for 50 concurrent users (p50/p95/p99)
- Streaming token latency breakdown and per-token cost estimate
- A basic test plan so our infra team can reproduce results in our staging VPC
- Recommended capacity/instance sizing for our peak (approx. 200 concurrent chat sessions, avg. 120 tokens/response)

We want to align on a close timeline: budget approval scheduled for Mar 24, so ideally we have the MAP and perf benchmarks in the next 10 business days. Can you confirm?

Thanks,
Raj

Date: 2026-03-07T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Initial profiling results — TTFT & streaming (attached)

Forwarding initial profiling run we kicked off against Redwood-hosted endpoint. Summary below; full charts are in attached PDF (ttft_streaming_results.pdf).

Summary (profiling harness config: 4 x g5-4dn, model: open-chat-30B-quant, seq_out=120, prompt_mean=80):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token):
  - 1 concurrent: p50=85ms, p95=140ms, p99=210ms
  - 10 concurrent: p50=95ms, p95=170ms, p99=260ms
  - 50 concurrent: p50=120ms, p95=240ms, p99=420ms
  - 200 concurrent (burst emulation): p50=220ms, p95=420ms, p99=950ms
- Streaming per-token latency (time between token emissions after first token):
  - p50=12ms/token, p95=28ms/token, p99=60ms/token (measured at 50 concurrent)
- End-to-end median throughput: ~55 tokens/sec per GPU for this model/config
- Observations:
  - KV cache hit helps for short-turn dialogues; prefix/reprompt patterns increase TTFT variance.
  - Network egress and TLS handshakes dominate a portion of TTFT at very low concurrencies; we recommend keep-alive and TLS session reuse in prod.

Attachments: ttft_streaming_results.pdf (report), raw_logs.tar.gz (attached for infra)

2) Did you measure with streaming enabled (chunked tokens) or with non-streaming (full response returned)?
3) Can we reproduce these results inside our VPC (expecting added latency)? Any guidance on margin to reserve?

We’re also trying to map these numbers into cost — can you add a quick per-session token cost at the recommended capacity?

Happy to get on a 30-min call if easier.

—Raj

Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial profiling results — TTFT & streaming (attached)

Raj — quick answers to your infra questions, happy to deep-dive on a call: 

1) Breakdown of p99 at 200 concurrent (950ms): approx. compute=420ms, queueing/serialization=300ms, network/TLS=230ms. These are approximate from our profiling traces (see ttft_streaming_results.pdf pages 7–9).
2) Measurements were taken with streaming enabled; per-token emission measured as streaming pipelined outputs. Non-streaming end-to-end latency is higher by ~60–120ms depending on buffer size.
3) In-VPC reproduction: expect additional 20–60ms of outbound network variance depending on cross-region hops and NAT Gateway overhead. We recommend running the Docker harness in your staging VPC to capture your egress behavior — we included exact env vars in test_plan_jan-qa.csv.

Cost notes: at 120 tokens/response avg and 200 concurrent sustained, our capacity recommendation (~10 GPUs) yields estimated cost per 1k responses: $X (we included a cost sheet in the MAP, see acme_map_v2.xlsx). We can run a detailed cost-sensitivity run if you want.

If you’re aiming for 500ms p99 TTFT we can propose two options:
- Option A (low-lift): keep streaming, add low-latency instance types + TLS session reuse + local edge proxy to reduce network component — target p99 ~450ms, moderate cost increase.
- Option B (aggressive): reserve dedicated GPUs, pin model instance warm pools and pre-warm KV cache; target p99 < 350ms, higher cost and operational complexity.

Connor O'Brien
Customer Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com
